config.title: Cost optimisation

intro.title: Cost optimisation
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple cost monitoring dashboard that visualizes cloud service expenses over time. You'll learn how to implement cost optimization by analyzing usage data and identifying potential savings. The core concepts include data visualization, basic cost analysis, and resource efficiency principles. You'll work with simulated cost data and use fundamental production engineering tools to track and optimize spending. This hands-on project will help you understand how to reduce operational costs while maintaining system performance.
intro.usecase: Cost optimization is critical in production engineering for managing cloud infrastructure expenses. Developers implement this through resource monitoring dashboards that track spending across services like AWS EC2 or Azure VMs. These dashboards feature interactive panels showing usage trends, cost alerts, and optimization recommendations. Engineers use these tools to right-size instances, schedule auto-scaling, and eliminate idle resources, directly impacting operational budgets.

objectives: Implement a cost monitoring dashboard to visualize resource usage
Configure auto-scaling rules to adjust resources based on demand
Apply tagging strategies to categorize and track cloud expenditures
Construct budget alerts to notify when spending exceeds thresholds
Manipulate instance types and sizes to match workload requirements
Integrate reserved instance purchases to reduce long-term costs
Update storage policies to archive or delete unused data

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package to enable state management in the cost optimization component.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and useState for state management
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are imported, making them available for use in the component.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import both React and the useState hook from the 'react' package to proceed.

steps.title: Create the CostOptimization component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named CostOptimization that returns an empty div element.
steps.hint: Define a function called CostOptimization that returns JSX containing a <div> element.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the CostOptimization component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named CostOptimization is defined and returns an empty div element.
successCriteria: The component is named CostOptimization and returns a <div> element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named exactly 'CostOptimization' and returns a <div> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Check that you defined a function named CostOptimization that returns a <div>.

steps.title: Initialize cost optimization state
steps.instruction: Inside your CostOptimization component, initialize three state variables using useState: currentCost (number), optimizedCost (number), and optimizationEnabled (boolean). Set their initial values to 100, 80, and false respectively.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. Each useState call should have an appropriate initial value: a number for costs, a boolean for enabled status.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have three state variables ready to track cost data and optimization status.
successCriteria: The component contains three useState calls with the specified variable names and initial values: currentCost (100), optimizedCost (80), and optimizationEnabled (false).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've initialized some state variables, but check that you have all three: currentCost, optimizedCost, and optimizationEnabled with the correct initial values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization is missing or incorrect. Make sure to use useState to create three variables with the specified names and initial values.

steps.title: Define cost calculation helper function
steps.instruction: Inside your CostOptimization component, define a function named calculateOptimizedCost that takes a currentCost parameter and returns an optimized cost (for example, 80% of the current cost).
steps.hint: Create a function that performs a calculation on the input parameter and returns the result.
steps.expectedOutcome: A calculateOptimizedCost function is defined inside the component, ready to be used for cost optimization calculations.
successCriteria: The calculateOptimizedCost function is defined, takes a currentCost parameter, and returns a calculated optimized cost value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started defining the function, but make sure it takes a parameter and returns a calculated value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The calculateOptimizedCost function isn't properly defined yet. Remember to create a function that takes a currentCost parameter and returns an optimized cost calculation.

steps.title: Define optimization toggle handler
steps.instruction: Define a function named toggleOptimization inside your CostOptimization component that toggles the optimizationEnabled state and calculates the optimized cost when enabled.
steps.hint: Create a function that sets optimizationEnabled to its opposite value using the setter function, then calls calculateOptimizedCost when optimizationEnabled becomes true.
steps.expectedOutcome: A toggleOptimization function is defined that toggles the optimizationEnabled state and calls calculateOptimizedCost when optimization is enabled.
successCriteria: The toggleOptimization function is defined, toggles the optimizationEnabled state using its setter, and calls calculateOptimizedCost when optimizationEnabled becomes true.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined the toggleOptimization function, but make sure it properly toggles the state and calls calculateOptimizedCost when optimization is enabled.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggleOptimization function is missing or doesn't properly toggle the optimizationEnabled state and call calculateOptimizedCost when needed.

steps.title: Define cost update handler
steps.instruction: Inside the CostOptimization component, define a function named updateCurrentCost that takes a new cost value as a parameter, updates the currentCost state, and recalculates optimized cost if optimization is enabled.
steps.hint: The function should accept a parameter (e.g., newCost), call setCurrentCost with that value, and conditionally call calculateOptimizedCost if optimizationEnabled is true.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function updateCurrentCost is defined that updates currentCost state and conditionally recalculates optimized cost.
successCriteria: The updateCurrentCost function is defined, accepts a parameter, updates currentCost state, and conditionally calls calculateOptimizedCost.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but ensure it updates currentCost state and conditionally calls calculateOptimizedCost when optimization is enabled.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Make sure to create updateCurrentCost that updates state and conditionally recalculates optimized cost.

steps.title: Add main container and title
steps.instruction: Inside the CostOptimization component, add a main container div with a title element displaying 'Cost Optimization Dashboard'.
steps.hint: Return a div element containing an h1 element with the specified text.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component returns a div container with an h1 title.
successCriteria: A div element containing an h1 element with the text 'Cost Optimization Dashboard' is returned.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have a div containing an h1 with the exact text 'Cost Optimization Dashboard'.

steps.title: Display current and optimized costs
steps.instruction: Add two paragraph elements inside the main container to display the currentCost and optimizedCost state values with descriptive labels.
steps.hint: Use JSX curly braces to embed the state values within the paragraph text.
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show two labeled paragraphs displaying the current and optimized cost values.
successCriteria: Two paragraph elements are added with labels and the currentCost and optimizedCost state values displayed.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added paragraphs, but make sure both currentCost and optimizedCost are displayed with appropriate labels.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires adding two paragraph elements to display the currentCost and optimizedCost state values.

steps.title: Add cost input and wire to update handler
steps.instruction: Inside the component's return statement, add an input field for the current cost and wire its onChange event to the updateCurrentCost handler function.
steps.hint: Use an <input> element with type='number' and set its onChange prop to call updateCurrentCost with the event's target value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: input field with onChange handler
<input type="number" onChange={(e) => updateValue(e.target.value)} />
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have an interactive input field that allows users to update the current cost value.
successCriteria: An input element with type='number' is added to the return statement, and its onChange event is wired to call updateCurrentCost with the event's target value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an input field, but make sure to wire the onChange event properly to updateCurrentCost with the event's target value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input field is missing or not properly connected to the update handler. Check that you've added an <input> element with type='number' and an onChange handler.

steps.title: Add optimization toggle button and wire to handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside the main container that toggles optimization when clicked. Wire its onClick event to the toggleOptimization handler function.
steps.hint: Create a <button> element with an onClick prop that calls toggleOptimization. Add appropriate text content like 'Toggle Optimization'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: button with click handler
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will now have a functional button that users can click to toggle optimization settings.
successCriteria: A button element is added to the component
The button's onClick prop calls toggleOptimization
The button has appropriate text content
